367410.title: Turán bound for suspensions of arbitrary trees
367410.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree whose smaller color class has size $k$, and let $\widehat{T}$ denote the suspension of $T$. Let $f(n,k)$ be the bound defined earlier in the paper. **Conjecture on suspensions of trees.** For large $n$,

$$
{\rm ex}(n,\widehat{T})\le f(n,k).
$$

The paper proves the result for balanced trees and notes that the same conclusion would follow for certain unbalanced trees if the relevant decomposition lemma holds. The conjecture asks whether the bound extends to every tree, and the source gives no resolution.
367410.source_name: Xiutao Zhu, Xiaolin Wang, Yanbo Zhang and Fangfang Zhang, “Turán problems for suspension of a balanced tree”, arXiv:2503.05166 (2025).
367410.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.05166

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

367548.title: The unboundedness conjecture for glued posets
367548.statement: Let $\mathcal P_1$ and $\mathcal P_2$ be finite posets, and let $\mathcal P_2*\mathcal P_1$ denote their gluing, obtained by placing every element of $\mathcal P_1$ below every element of $\mathcal P_2$. Let $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\mathcal P)$ denote the induced saturation number. **Glued-poset unboundedness conjecture.** The function $\operatorname{sat}^*(n,\mathcal P_2*\mathcal P_1)$ is unbounded if and only if at least one of $\mathcal P_1$ and $\mathcal P_2$ has unbounded saturation number. This would extend the paper's established result in the case where at least one glued poset has the unique cover twin property.
367548.source_name: Maria-Romina Ivan and Sean Jaffe, “Gluing Posets and the Dichotomy of Poset Saturation Numbers”, arXiv:2503.12223 (2026).
367548.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12223

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

367636.title: Converse characterization of the essential approximate point spectrum for elliptic and double parabolic Blaschke products
367636.statement:
Let $B$ be an elliptic or double parabolic Blaschke product of degree $d \geq 2$, and let $T$ be the weighted composition operator on the disc algebra associated with $B$ and a weight $w$. Consider the set of moduli of scalars whose circles lie in the upper semi-Fredholm spectrum:

$$
\{\lvert\lambda\rvert: \lambda \mathds{T} \subset \sigma_{usf}(T)\}.
$$

**Converse characterization conjecture.** The set $\{\lvert\lambda\rvert: \lambda \mathds{T} \subset \sigma_{usf}(T)\}$ is at most countable and its only accumulation point, if any, is $0$.

The surrounding discussion presents this as the converse to the preceding theorem for finite Blaschke products. The supplied text does not establish the converse, so its resolution remains open.
367636.source_name: Arkady Kitover and Mehmet Orhon, “Spectrum of weighted composition operators. Part XI. The essential spectra of some weighted composition operators on the disc algebra”, arXiv:2503.17516 (2025).
367636.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.17516

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2025).

367655.title: Pruesse–Ruskey Hamiltonicity conjecture for Venn-diagram graphs
367655.statement:
For an $n$-Venn diagram, consider the graph whose vertices are the crossings of the curves and whose edges are the curve segments between consecutive crossings; this graph may have multiple edges. **Pruesse and Ruskey's conjecture.** For $n\geq 2$, the graph of any (not necessarily simple) $n$-Venn diagram has a Hamilton cycle.

Pruesse and Ruskey proved the corresponding statement for simple Venn diagrams, using 4-connectivity and Tutte's theorem. The conjecture asks whether Hamiltonicity continues to hold for non-simple Venn diagrams; this paper is concerned with disproving such conjectures.
367655.source_name: Sofia Brenner, Linda Kleist, Torsten Mütze, Christian Rieck and Francesco Verciani, “Disproving two conjectures on the Hamiltonicity of Venn diagrams”, arXiv:2503.18554 (2026).
367655.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.18554

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2025). “The conjecture is also listed as the first open problem in Ruskey and Weston's inspiring survey on Venn diagrams.”

367774.title: The linear-forest conjecture for intersectionwise self-$\chi$-guarding graph classes
367774.statement:
A **linear forest** is a forest in which every component is a path. For a graph $H$, an $H$-free graph is a graph with no induced subgraph isomorphic to $H$; a class is intersectionwise self-$\chi$-guarding when it has the property defined in the paper.

**Linear-forest conjecture.** If $H$ is a linear forest, then the class of $H$-free graphs is intersectionwise self-$\chi$-guarding.

The preceding results establish this property for stars and for $P_{4}$-free graphs, while the paper's corollary shows that any graph $H$ whose $H$-free class is intersectionwise self-$\chi$-guarding must be a linear forest or a star. The conjecture addresses the remaining linear-forest cases.
367774.source_name: Aristotelis Chaniotis, Hidde Koerts and Sophie Spirkl, “Intersections of graphs and χ-boundedness”, arXiv:2504.00153 (2025).
367774.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00153

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

367788.title: Hypergeometric rationality conjecture for unicellular Ising maps with few monochromatic edges
367788.statement:
Let $U_{n,i,j}$ denote the coefficient of $t^{3n}\nu_{\bullet}^i\nu_{\circ}^j$ in the generating series $U$ for unicellular Ising maps, and set $n=2g-1$.

**Few-monochromatic-edges conjecture.** For fixed $i,j\geq 0$, there exists a rational function $Q_{i,j}(g)$ in $g$ such that

$$
U_{n,i,j}=Q_{i,j}(g)\frac{(2g)!(3g)!}{3^g g!^3}.
$$

These numbers vanish when $i-j$ is not a multiple of $3$.

This conjecture concerns the opposite regime from maps with many monochromatic edges. The source gives several predicted instances, but no proof of the general rational-function form is provided.
367788.source_name: Mireille Bousquet-Mélou, Ariane Carrance and Baptiste Louf, “The Ising model on cubic maps: arbitrary genus”, arXiv:2504.00768 (2025).
367788.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00768

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

367789.title: Helme-Guizon–Przytycki–Rong torsion conjecture for chromatic homology
367789.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph, and let ${{H_{*,*}}^{\mathcal{A}_m}(G)}$ denote its chromatic cohomology over the algebra $\mathcal{A}_m$. A graph has a loop if it contains an edge whose endpoints coincide, and a cycle has order equal to its number of edges.

**Helme-Guizon–Przytycki–Rong torsion conjecture.** The cohomology ${{H_{*,*}}^{\mathcal{A}_m}(G)}$ contains a torsion part if and only if $G$ has no loops and contains a cycle of order at least $3$. In this case, ${{H_{*,*}}^{\mathcal{A}_m}(G)}$ has torsion of order dividing $m$.

This conjecture concerns the existence and order of torsion in chromatic homology over $\mathcal{A}_m$. The supplied text identifies it as a conjecture posed by Helme-Guizon, Przytycki, and Rong, but gives no resolution status.
367789.source_name: Aninda Banerjee, Apratim Chakraborty, Swarup Kumar Das and Pravakar Paul, “A spanning tree model for chromatic homology”, arXiv:2504.00834 (2025).
367789.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00834

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

367794.title: The balanced separator conjecture for sphere intersection graphs
367794.statement:
Let $t,d
greater than or equal to 1$ be integers, and let $G$ be an $n$-vertex graph in the class $\SphereInt{d}_t$ of sphere intersection graphs. A balanced separator is a vertex set whose removal leaves no connected component with more than a fixed balanced fraction of the vertices. **Balanced separator conjecture.** Every such graph has a balanced separator of size

$$
{\bigO{}}_{t,d}(n^{1-\frac{1}{d+1}}).
$$

The conjecture would improve the exponent in the known separator theorem for sphere intersection graphs. It is known for $d=1$, while the general case remains open.
367794.source_name: James Davies, Agelos Georgakopoulos, Meike Hatzel and Rose McCarty, “Strongly sublinear separators and bounded asymptotic dimension for sphere intersection graphs”, arXiv:2504.00932 (2025).
367794.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.00932

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of April 2025). “The case $d=2$ of the conjecture (furthermore for Assouad--Nagata dimension and in the more general class of string graphs) will be proved in separate work .”

367832.title: Finite four-point obstruction conjecture for labeled star graph ultrametric spaces
367832.statement:
Let $(X^*,d^*)$ be a finite ultrametric space. The space $X^*$ is a **US-space** when it belongs to the class ${\bf US}$ of ultrametric spaces generated by labeled star graphs. A four-point subspace is **weakly similar** to another metric space when there is a similarity between them, allowing a positive rescaling of the distance. **Finite four-point obstruction conjecture.** The following statements are equivalent:

1. $(X^*,d^*) \notin {\bf US}$.
2. $(X^*,d^*)$ contains a four-point subspace which is weakly similar either to $(X_4,d_4)$ or to $(Y_4,\rho_4)$.

This conjecture proposes that the two displayed four-point spaces are the complete finite obstructions to membership in ${\bf US}$; its resolution is not supplied in the source.
367832.source_name: Oleksiy Dovgoshey, Omer Cantor and Olga Rovenska, “Compact ultrametric spaces generated by labeled star graphs”, arXiv:2504.02425 (2025).
367832.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.02425

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

367984.title: The internal-degree conjecture for one-crossing triangulation graphs
367984.statement:
Let ${\cal C}_0$ consist of graphs obtained from 4-connected plane triangulations by choosing distinct facial triangles $xuv$ and $yuv$ sharing the edge $uv$ and adding the edge $xy$. The vertices $x,y,u,v$ are called **external**, and all other vertices are called **internal**.

**Internal-degree conjecture.** Every non-4-colorable graph in ${\cal C}_0$ has an internal vertex of degree four.

The source presents this as an equivalent form of the strong one-crossing 4-coloring conjecture, reflecting the reduction to triangulated configurations; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
367984.source_name: Zdeněk Dvořák, Bernard Lidický and Bojan Mohar, “On a conjecture concerning 4-coloring of graphs with one crossing”, arXiv:2504.08327 (2025).
367984.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.08327

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

368114.title: Anastos–Fabian–Müyesser–Szabó conjecture for three disjoint perfect matchings
368114.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $2n$ vertices that is the union of three disjoint perfect matchings. An **$(a_1,a_2,a_3)$-matching** is a matching containing exactly $a_i$ edges from the $i$th perfect matching. Suppose that $G$ has a component that is not isomorphic to $K_4$. **Anastos–Fabian–Müyesser–Szabó conjecture.** For any integers $a_1,a_2,a_3\in\mathbb{N}_0$ satisfying

$$
a_1+a_2+a_3=n-1,
$$

$G$ contains an $(a_1,a_2,a_3)$-matching. This removes the known obstruction formed by a disjoint union of copies of $K_4$ and asks whether that is the only obstruction; the paper reiterates it as an open conjecture.
368114.source_name: Simona Boyadzhiyska, Micha Christoph and Tibor Szabó, “Almost-perfect colorful matchings in three-edge-colored bipartite graphs”, arXiv:2504.15167 (2025).
368114.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.15167

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

368164.title: The claw-free four-perfect-matching conjecture
368164.statement:
A cubic graph is **claw-free** if it has no induced subgraph isomorphic to $K_{1,3}$. A set of perfect matchings **covers** a graph when every edge belongs to at least one matching. **Claw-free four-perfect-matching conjecture.** Every claw-free bridgeless cubic graph can be covered with four perfect matchings.

The paper states that this conjecture is equivalent to the 5-cycle double cover conjecture. Consequently, it remains open.
368164.source_name: Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo and Vahan Mkrtchyan, “Expanding vertices to triangles in cubic graphs”, arXiv:2504.19201 (2025).
368164.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19201

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

368169.title: Equivalence of the 3/5 and 2/5 5-cycle double cover bounds
368169.statement:
Let $G$ be a bridgeless graph, and let a $5$-cycle double cover be a collection ${\cal C}=(E_0,\ldots,E_4)$ of five cycles in which every edge belongs to exactly two cycles. **Equivalence conjecture for strengthened 5-cycle double covers.** The conjecture asserting that every bridgeless graph admits such a cover with

$$
|E_0|\geq \frac{3}{5}|E(G)|
$$

is equivalent to the conjecture asserting that every bridgeless graph admits such a cover with

$$
|E_0|\geq \frac{2}{5}|E(G)|.
$$

The paper says that the $2/5$ formulation is equivalent to the ordinary 5-cycle double cover conjecture and proposes the equivalence with the strengthened formulation. It remains open.
368169.source_name: Giuseppe Mazzuoccolo and Vahan Mkrtchyan, “Expanding vertices to triangles in cubic graphs”, arXiv:2504.19201 (2025).
368169.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2504.19201

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2025).

368265.title: Nonexistence conjecture for face-transitive Klein bottles
368265.statement: A **face-transitive Klein bottle** is a simplicial Klein bottle whose face-transitive symmetry property is understood in the sense of the paper's census. **Face-transitive Klein bottle conjecture.** There is no face-transitive Klein bottle. The conjecture arises from the census: no non-orientable face-transitive surface in the computed list has Euler characteristic $0$, the Euler characteristic of the Klein bottle, but the general nonexistence claim remains open.
368265.source_name: Reymond Akpanya and Jonathan Spreer, “A census of face-transitive surfaces”, arXiv:2505.00425 (2025).
368265.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00425

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

368277.title: Generic first-order rigidity conjecture for combinatorial types of convex polytopes
368277.statement: Let $\mathcal P$ be the combinatorial type of a convex polytope of dimension $d\geq 3$. **Generic first-order rigidity conjecture.** If $\mathcal P$ is the combinatorial type of a convex polytope of dimension $d\geq 3$, then $\mathcal P$ is generically (first-order) rigid. This is the precise formulation of generic rigidity used in the paper. The conjecture is proved for $d=3$, whereas it remains open for $d\geq 4$.
368277.source_name: Matthias Himmelmann, Bernd Schulze and Martin Winter, “Rigidity of polytopes with edge length and coplanarity constraints”, arXiv:2505.00874 (2026).
368277.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.00874

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2025). “Although remains open for $d\ge 4$, we will discuss potential approaches in .”

368314.title: Signed-cardinality homomesy conjecture for interval-closed sets of products of two chains
368314.statement:
Let $[m]\times[n]$ be the product of two chains, and let an interval-closed set mean a subset that is interval-closed in this poset. For $x\in[m]\times[n]$, define the signed cardinality by the parity of its rank, and for an interval-closed set $I$ let $\mathrm{sc}(I)$ be the sum of these signs over $I$. A statistic is $0$-mesic if its average on every rowmotion orbit is zero. **Signed-cardinality homomesy conjecture.** If $m=2$ or $m=3$, then the signed cardinality statistic is $0$-mesic under rowmotion on interval-closed sets of $[m]\times[n]$ whenever $m+n-1$ is even.

The conjecture extends homomesy results for ordinal sums of antichains and the known $[2]\times[n]$ case; the source states that its $m=2$ case is proved by the paper's Theorem 1. The $m=3$ case remains unresolved here.
368314.source_name: Nadia Lafrenière, Joel Brewster Lewis, Erin McNicholas, Jessica Striker and Amanda Welch, “Interval-closed set rowmotion and homomesy on products of two chains”, arXiv:2505.04000 (2025).
368314.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.04000

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

368382.title: Colbourn's conjecture on realizations under a largest-part bound
368382.statement:
Let $(h_1\dots h_k)$ be a partition with $h_1\geq\dots\geq h_k>0$, and let an **RP** be a realization of a partition by disjoint subsquares of a Latin square. **Colbourn's conjecture.** If

$$
k\geq 5\quad\text{and}\quad 0<h_1\leq (k-2)h_k,
$$

then an $\operatorname{RP}(h_1\dots h_k)$ exists.

This is the second unconditional-existence family conjectured by Colbourn. It extends the known results on realizations with few subsquares or with at most two distinct part sizes; no resolution of the full stated range is given here.
368382.source_name: Tara Kemp and James Lefevre, “Further results on latin squares with disjoint subsquares using rational outline squares”, arXiv:2505.07252 (2025).
368382.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.07252

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

368492.title: Generalised Common Neighbour Conjecture for Saxl hypergraphs
368492.statement: Let $G\leq \operatorname{Sym}(\Omega)$ be a finite permutation group with base size $b(G)\geq 2$, and let $\mathcal{H}(G)$ be its Saxl hypergraph; in the original graph formulation, use $\Sigma(G)$. **Generalised Common Neighbour Conjecture.** For any distinct points $\alpha,\beta\in\Omega$, there exist a third point $\gamma\in\Omega\setminus\{\alpha,\beta\}$ and edges $E_\alpha,E_\beta$ of $\mathcal{H}(G)$ such that $\alpha,\gamma\in E_\alpha$ and $\beta,\gamma\in E_\beta$. This formulation generalises the common-neighbour property from Saxl graphs to Saxl hypergraphs; the supplied source gives no resolution.
368492.source_name: Melissa Lee and Anthony Pisani, “The Saxl hypergraph of a permutation group”, arXiv:2505.13849 (2025).
368492.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.13849

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2025).

368836.title: The clique-cutset conjecture for minimally non-perfectly divisible graphs
368836.statement:
Let $G$) be a graph. A graph is **perfectly divisible** if every induced subgraph with at least one edge has a partition $(A,B)$ such that the induced graph on $A$ is perfect and $(G[B])<(G)$. A graph is **minimally non-perfectly divisible** (MNPD) if it is not perfectly divisible but every proper induced subgraph is perfectly divisible. A **clique cutset** is a clique whose deletion disconnects $G$.

**Clique-cutset conjecture.** No MNPD graph contains a clique cutset.

This conjecture is proposed as an analogue of the folklore result that no minimal imperfect graph contains a clique cutset. Its status is open.
368836.source_name: Chính T. Hoàng, “On the structure of perfectly divisible graphs”, arXiv:2506.12660 (2025).
368836.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12660

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).

368837.title: The P5-free perfect divisibility conjecture
368837.statement:
Let $P_5$ denote the chordless path on five vertices. A graph is **perfectly divisible** if every induced subgraph with at least one edge has a partition $(A,B)$ such that the induced graph on $A$ is perfect and $(G[B])<(G)$.

**P5-free conjecture.** Every $P_5$-free graph is perfectly divisible.

The conjecture is proposed in connection with the paper's clique-cutset results. Chudnovsky and Sivaraman proved the related result that $(P_5,\operatorname{bull})$-free graphs are perfectly divisible; the stated conjecture remains open.
368837.source_name: Chính T. Hoàng, “On the structure of perfectly divisible graphs”, arXiv:2506.12660 (2025).
368837.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.12660

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2025).
